theory.intro: The area of a rectangle is the amount of surface it covers, found by multiplying its length by its width.
facts: Area is measured in square units: cm$^2$, m$^2$, km$^2$.
A square is a rectangle with equal sides, so its area is **side $\times$ side**.
steps: Read the length and the width (use the same unit for both).
Write the answer with squared units.

foundation.question_text: A rectangular vegetable garden is $8\text{ m}$ long and $3\text{ m}$ wide. Find the area of the garden in $\text{m}^{2}$.

development.solution_text:
The equal tick marks show the shape is a square, so both dimensions are $9\text{ mm}$.
$A=9\times9$
$=81\text{ mm}^{2}$

$=36\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{B}}=6\times6$
$=36\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger: both shapes have an area of $36\text{ cm}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text: A rectangle measures $6\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$. Both the length and the width are doubled. Find the area of the new rectangle in $\text{cm}^{2}$, and state how many times as large it is as the original.
mastery.solution_text:
$A_{\text{old}}=6\times5$
$=30\text{ cm}^{2}$
New dimensions: $12\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$.
$A_{\text{new}}=12\times10$
$=120\text{ cm}^{2}$
$120\div30=4$
The new area is $120\text{ cm}^{2}$, which is $4$ times the original.

mastery.question_text: A rectangular courtyard is $12\text{ m}$ long and $7.5\text{ m}$ wide. It is to be covered with rectangular pavers measuring $0.5\text{ m}$ by $0.3\text{ m}$. How many pavers are needed?

A rectangle has length $10\text{ cm}$ and width $6\text{ cm}$. Its length is then increased by $2\text{ cm}$ and its width decreased by $2\text{ cm}$. Find both areas in $\text{cm}^{2}$ and state whether the area is unchanged.
mastery.solution_text:
$A_{\text{old}}=10\times6$
$=60\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{new}}=12\times4$
$=48\text{ cm}^{2}$
The area is not unchanged: it falls by $12\text{ cm}^{2}$.
